DATE RECEIVED: [redacted]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile X syndrome in pediatric male patient.

METHODOLOGY
PCR-based assay for detection of CGG repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene promoter region. This test detects the number of CGG repeats in the 5' untranslated region of the FMR1 gene associated with Fragile X syndrome. The assay utilizes fluorescent PCR amplification with capillary electrophoresis for accurate sizing of CGG repeat alleles.

RESULTS
FMR1 CGG Repeat Analysis:
Allele: 29 (+/-1) CGG repeats
Classification: NORMAL

Reference Ranges:
Normal: 6-45 CGG repeats
Intermediate: 46-54 CGG repeats
Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

INTERPRETATION
A normal allele with 29 (+/-1) CGG repeats was detected in the FMR1 gene. No expansion allele is present. This result indicates that the patient is very unlikely to be affected with Fragile X syndrome based on the normal repeat size detected.

LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based assay specifically detects CGG repeat expansions in the FMR1 gene. A small percentage (<1%) of Fragile X syndrome cases may result from point mutations or other rearrangements within the FMR1 gene that are not detected by this method. If clinical suspicion remains high, additional testing such as FMR1 gene sequencing may be considered.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
